_comment: A small dedicated ruin map (Albez-flavored surface ruin), sized identically to `sewers` (20x14, biome `cave` reused as the stone-floor default -- data/biomes.json is not touched here, so every new map must reuse an existing biome id; `cave` gives the rocky/rubble read an Albez ruin wants). Entered ONLY from floodplains' `ruin_door` (door_when-gated); the sole exit is `ruin_exit` below, landing back at floodplains (37,11) -- one cell west of `ruin_door`'s own (38,11) cell, the sewer_exit/deep_fissure 'never land on the door's own cell' convention. Reachability: (2,2) [the door_when to_cell] -> open floor the whole way east to the guardian alcove at (16-18,5-7); two decorative rubble piles (5,4)/(13,9) sit off that direct line and off any reasonable perimeter walk. `anchor_stone_pedestal` (17,6) is reachable from all four neighbor cells; `ruin_guardian` (17,8) stands one cell south of the pedestal's own south neighbor, 'guarding' it in the fiction without physically sealing any approach (see that entity's own _comment for the sprite-fusion fix that placed it there). The pedestal ships LOCKED-FLAVOR (see that prop's own _comment for the full container-gating rationale) rather than the `contains` shape wired once the alternate TALK/SKILL gates land. Mood card `ruin_surface` (data/moods.json) is a tuned cold-daylight/dusty grade, day/dusk/night graded (a SURFACE ruin sees real weather, unlike the sewers/deep_tunnels time-invariant pins).

walls._comment: Every other cave-biome map (sewers/deep_tunnels) carries interior obstacle dressing via walls.segments even with NO perimeter enclosure (grid-bound clipping alone stops movement at the map edge; segments here are INTERIOR texture/blocking, matching deep_tunnels' stalactite-rubble/fallen-column precedent -- from/to only, no cap/face, same minimal shape). Both segments sit in the untouched middle of the room (x6-11, y8-11), clear of ruin_walkthrough's own leg-by-leg cell audit (top row y=2 x2-17; column x=17 y2-5; row y=5 x2-17; column x=2 y5-13; bottom row y=13 x2-19; column x=19 y1-13; row y=1 x3-19) and both existing `blocked` singletons (5,4)/(13,9) -- no re-derivation of that script's route needed; re-verified live (ruin_walkthrough passes unchanged).

segments._comment: A fallen ceiling rubble column, Albez-ruin dressing.

floor_layers._pick: ruin floor, reusing the verified cave-floor tile neighborhood (Albez-flavored rubble/stone read).

entities._comment: The way back up -- returns to floodplains beside `ruin_door` (38,11); see that entity's own _comment for the full placement/blast-radius disclosure. Landing cell (2,2) is one cell south of this door, matching the sewer_exit/deep_fissure 'the way back up' convention.

The beat-3 recovery target. Gated by src/core/wi_game.gd's interact()/_interact_container (the door_when-style `contains_when: {requires: {...}}` gate, reusing `_door_gate_met` verbatim, no separate gate logic). Gated on `pedestal_unsealed` (an internal convergence counter): banked by EITHER `cleared_ruin_guardian` (fight him right here) OR any of Pisces's TALK/SKILL mage-consult legs (their examination doubles as safe-passage insight -- the FIGHT-at-beat-2 leg, having sent the player to clear `rift_vermin_leak` in the inn instead, does NOT bank it, so THOSE players still have to clear the guardian in person; see that entity's own _comment below). `on_interact_accomplishment`/`toast` KEPT verbatim as the unmet-gate fallback (interact()'s new contains_when check falls through to this exact branch when unmet -- ruin_walkthrough's fixture has door_chain_started but neither pedestal_unsealed producer, so its locked-toast assertion is untouched, byte-identical). `on_open_accomplishment: recovered_anchor_stone` (the chain's locked id) fires once, on the SAME interact that grants the item, the first time the gate is met.
entities.observe: A stone rests in a shallow cradle atop the plinth, held there by nothing you can see. Something older than the dust stands close enough to notice you noticing.
entities.toast: The stone doesn't move. Whatever holds it there is still standing guard, close enough that reaching for it feels like a very bad idea.

entities._comment: The real `kind: "encounter"` shape (ruin_guardian/ruin_ward_a/ruin_ward_b in data/combatants.json, the `ruin_court` arena in data/arenas.json). Locked ids: arena `ruin_court`, enemies EXACTLY ["ruin_guardian","ruin_ward_a","ruin_ward_b"] (the entity id and the first enemy combatant id are both `ruin_guardian` by design -- separate registries, entities vs. combatants, no collision), on_victory banks `cleared_ruin_guardian` + the shared `pedestal_unsealed` convergence counter (see `anchor_stone_pedestal`'s own _comment for the full OR-gate rationale). `allies:["relc"]`/`ally_requires:{met_relc:1}` matches the harness's gated cell (`ruin_guardian_w8_relc`, the tuned 0.55-0.8 band) over the harder ungated `_solo` variant. `on_interact_accomplishment`/`toast` are dead fields on an encounter and stay unset; `observe` is kept. Placed at (17,8), one row south of the pedestal's immediate south approach -- keeps clear of a PC/guardian sprite-fusion bug at the canonical 2-cell viewing distance (`ruin_walkthrough`'s `01_pedestal_locked.png`, PC at (17,5)); the pedestal's 4 neighbor cells are all open floor, and the guardian still visibly stands in the same alcove, still the last thing between the player and the stone, just not a hard physical block on that one approach cell. CONTRACT: `door_chain_fight.json`'s teleport target must stay in sync at (16,8), the west-adjacent cell.
entities.observe: Stone shaped like a soldier, or close enough that the difference doesn't help you. It hasn't moved since you stepped into this room. That is not the same as harmless.
